subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: For plain provider messages like `LLM error api_error: Internal server error`, should OpenClaw treat them as shared provider cooldown signals, cron-local transient retry signals, or only generic timeouts with additional timing proof?
rationale: Current main already handles structured `server_error`, but plain internal-server text remains timeout-like; changing that policy affects cron recovery, fallback latency, and whether provider/profile health may be suppressed across other runs.

options.title: Cron-local transient server error
options.body: Classify the cron-visible plain internal-server text as retryable `server_error` for cron retry and failure-alert behavior without marking shared auth-profile cooldown.

options.title: Shared provider cooldown
options.body: Treat plain internal-server failures as provider outage signals that can skip same-provider candidates across runs, accepting broader cooldown effects.

options.title: Keep timeout-only with proof
options.body: Leave plain provider 500 text timeout-like only if focused cron/fallback tests prove the run fast-fails before the outer deadline.

recommendation.title: Cron-local transient server error
recommendation.body: Classify the cron-visible plain internal-server text as retryable `server_error` for cron retry and failure-alert behavior without marking shared auth-profile cooldown.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is a maintainer policy decision spanning cron, provider health, and fallback behavior, and steipete is the strongest human maintainer/area-routing signal in the checked history.
